name: Joash
bio:
Joash (Jehoash), son of Ahaziah, was an infant when his grandmother Athaliah seized the throne and tried to wipe out the royal line; his aunt Jehosheba stole him away and hid him in the temple with his nurse for six years. In the seventh year, the priest Jehoiada organized the temple guard, crowned and anointed Joash king inside the temple, and had Athaliah killed when she tried to stop it. Joash began to reign at seven years old (2 Kings 11:1-21).

## 📖 Core Story: Temple Repairs, Tribute to Hazael, and Assassination

Joash reigned forty years in Jerusalem, doing right in the LORD's eyes all the days Jehoiada the priest instructed him, though the high places remained. He ordered the priests to use dedicated and freewill temple money to repair the temple's damage, but by his twenty-third year, nothing had been done; Jehoiada then set a collection chest by the altar, and once it filled, the money was faithfully paid out to carpenters, builders, and masons until the temple was repaired, with the priests dealing honestly and no accounting demanded of them (2 Kings 12:1-15).

Chronicles adds that Jehoiada had arranged two wives for Joash, who fathered sons and daughters, and that when the temple repairs stalled, it was Joash himself who confronted Jehoiada over the Levites' delay, after which the collection chest was set up and the work completed with the leftover money used for temple vessels of gold and silver. Jehoiada lived to a remarkable old age, dying at 130, and was buried among the kings in the City of David for the good he had done for God and Judah — an honor denied to Joash himself. After Jehoiada's death, the officials of Judah won Joash over, and the people abandoned the temple to worship Asherah poles and idols; when the Spirit of God moved Jehoiada's own son Zechariah to rebuke the people for forsaking the LORD, Joash had him stoned to death in the temple courtyard itself, repaying Jehoiada's lifelong devotion with the murder of his son — Zechariah's dying words asked the LORD to call Joash to account for it (2 Chronicles 24:1-22).

When Hazael, king of Syria, captured Gath and set his sights on Jerusalem, Joash stripped the temple and his own palace of all their gold and dedicated treasures — including what his predecessors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah had dedicated — and sent it all to Hazael, who then withdrew from Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:17-18). Chronicles frames this same crisis as divine judgment: a small Aramean force defeated Judah's much larger army, killed the leading officials, and plundered the city, leaving Joash himself severely wounded. Joash was later assassinated by his own servants, Jozachar and Jehozabad, in the house of Millo (2 Kings 12:19-21) — named in 2 Chronicles 24:26 as Zabad, son of an Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad, son of a Moabite woman, who killed him in his bed in revenge for Zechariah's murder. He was buried in the City of David but, unlike his predecessors, not among the kings; his son Amaziah succeeded him.
